subject: ACME bake-off: draft test plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME bake-off: draft test plan & next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs (from our call)
- Primary goal: 95th pct latency < 300ms for chat-style LLMs (max seq 1024) and cost target ~ $0.0008/token for production throughput.
- Workloads: mixed chat + embeddings-based retrieval reranking for search relevance tests.
- Compliance: SOC2 + VPC isolation for test data.

What we propose for the competitive bake-off
1) Scope: compare Redwood hosted inference vs. a major hyperscaler API and one open-hosted inference provider across the two canonical workloads (chat generation + embedding/re-ranker).
2) Success criteria: latency (p50/p95), throughput at target latency, per-token cost, output quality on your eval set (R@10 for reranking, ROUGE/semantic similarity for generative tasks).
3) Test plan & timeline: attach a draft spreadsheet with tests, owners, and timelines. Our suggested cadence: kickoff this week, run bench tests next week, quality evals week after, decision review w/ Acme on 7/8.
4) Owners: Redwood SE (Aditya) owns runtime benchmarks; Vanessa will coordinate billing/quoting and infra; I’ll own the QA & rollout plan.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.xlsx (draft)

Immediate asks for Acme: 
- Can you confirm the test dataset (we discussed synthetic + 1k anonymized real queries)? If you can share a ~1000-line sample, we will run the initial pass.
- Confirm whether VPC network peering is required for the early stage or if an isolated S3 + signed URLs is acceptable.

Next steps
- If that plan looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with the SEs and your engineering leads (suggest: Thu 6/24 or Fri 6/25).

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Adding internal notes and proposed bench details. Team —

Thanks Marissa. I sketched out the runtime benchmark plan inside the spreadsheet (tab: runtime-bench). Key items I included:
- Test harness: 4 clients, sequence lengths [64, 256, 1024], batching ramp (1..16), KV-cache warm/cold runs.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tail latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens extrapolated.
- Baseline models: gp-large-v2 (hyperscaler), open-runner-13B (open provider), redwood-opt-13B-quantized (our recommended).
- Tokenization parity: I’ll run a quick tokenizer diff and include a mapping report so Acme can normalize scores.

Owners: I’ll run the runtime bench and prepare the perf report (target complete by 6/30). Vanessa — can you prepare the pricing model + quote for the Dedicated baseline and a hosted per-token estimate?

Questions: do we want to include a cold-start model startup test (first-request latency) or focus only on steady-state? My recommendation: include both — cold-start matters for their spiky user journeys.

Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Following up with a couple of logistical items from Redwood side:

2) Quoting: Preliminary hosted per-token estimate (ballpark): $0.0010/token for gp-large-v2 equivalent; Redwood optimized path estimated at $0.00065/token (dependent on batching+quantization). I’ll share a formal quote after we know the targeted throughput.
